sentence: This project builds a non-invasive AI tool that helps find oral cancer early and decide which patients need care.
This project studies how age-related methylation and behavior differ in mice living in standard lab conditions versus more natural conditions.
This project studies how environmental exposures affect human health, using environmental toxicology, epidemiology and exposure sciences.
This project tries to improve treatment for cancer and serious mental illness and to help more people receive tobacco cessation care.
This project tries to develop a therapy that overcomes treatment resistance in ocular vascular diseases such as diabetic retinopathy.
This project studies how heart muscle repairs itself in zebrafish, looking for matrix proteins linked to a transcriptional pathway.
This project tries to find out how the Epstein-Barr virus and human genetics together contribute to multiple sclerosis.
This project studies how posttranslational lysine modifications regulate chromatin, polyubiquitination and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase.
This project tests whether engineered regulatory T cells can limit the immune attack behind autoimmune diabetes.
This project builds models that use genetics and electronic medical records to predict which patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease develop cirrhosis.
This project studies how mental stress triggers sympathetic activation in women who have chest pain and coronary microvascular dysfunction.
This project gathers and checks data on the human virome and builds a database that combines results from many methods.
This project tries to find out what shapes adherence to HIV therapy and adds alcohol interventions to help people with HIV suppress the virus.
This project studies how the amino acid cysteine in the diet affects the intestine and its ability to regenerate tissue.
This project provides immune profiling of blood, bone marrow and tissue samples from cancer patients to understand cancer and how patients respond to treatment.
This project builds biomaterials that mimic natural tissues to understand how cells sense mechanical signals from their environment.
This project uses artificial intelligence to analyze medical imaging and studies DNA methylation changes to find osteoporosis earlier.
This project studies how germline stem cells compete in the fruit fly testis and what molecular mechanisms control that competition.
